Stationarization

The previous chapters derive all the equations necessary to solve for the steady-state and nonsteady-state equilibria of this model. However, because labor productivity is growing at rate gyg_ygy​ as can be seen in the firms’ production function (46) and the population is growing at rate g~n,t\tilde{g}_{n,t}g~​n,t​ as defined in (5), the model is not stationary. Different endogenous variables of the model are growing at different rates. We have already specified three potential budget closure rules (107), (108), and (110) using some combination of government spending GtG_tGt​ and transfers TRtTR_tTRt​ that stationarize the debt-to-GDP ratio.

Table 3 lists the definitions of stationary versions of all the endogenous variables. Variables with a ``  ^  \:\,\hat{}\,\:^‘’ signify stationary variables. The first column of variables are growing at the productivity growth rate gyg_ygy​. These variables are most closely associated with individual variables. The second column of variables are growing at the population growth rate g~n,t\tilde{g}_{n,t}g~​n,t​. These variables are most closely associated with population values. The third column of variables are growing at both the productivity growth rate gyg_ygy​ and the population growth rate g~n,t\tilde{g}_{n,t}g~​n,t​. These variables are most closely associated with aggregate variables. The last column shows that the interest rates rtr_trt​, rp,tr_{p,t}rp,t​ and rgov,tr_{gov,t}rgov,t​, and household labor supply nj,s,tn_{j,s,t}nj,s,t​ are already stationary.

The usual definition of equilibrium would be allocations and prices such that households optimize (23), (40), (41), and (42), firms optimize (49) and (50), and markets clear (122), (126), (127), (132), (133), and (135). In this chapter, we show how to stationarize each of these characterizing equations so that we can use our fixed point methods described in Sections Steady-state solution method and Stationary non-steady-state solution method of Chapter Equilibrium to solve for the equilibria in the steady-state and transition path equilibrium definitions.

Stationarized Government Equations¶

Each of the tax rate functions τs,tetr,xy\tau^{etr,xy}_{s,t}τs,tetr,xy​, τtetr,2\tau^{etr,2}_{t}τtetr,2​ τs,tmtrx\tau^{mtrx}_{s,t}τs,tmtrx​, τs,tmtry\tau^{mtry}_{s,t}τs,tmtry​, and τtmtrw\tau^{mtrw}_{t}τtmtrw​ is stationary. The total tax liability function taxj,s,ttax_{j,s,t}taxj,s,t​ is growing at the rate of labor productivity growth gyg_ygy​ This can be see by looking at the decomposition of the total tax liability function into the effective tax rate times total income (27). The effective tax rate function is stationary, and household income is growing at rate gyg_ygy​. So household total tax liability is stationarized by dividing both sides of the equation by egyte^{g_y t}egy​t.

Stationary aggregate universal basic income expenditure is found in one of two ways depending on how the individual UBI payments ubij,s,tubi_{j,s,t}ubij,s,t​ are modeled. In Section Universal basic income of Chapter Government, we discuss how UBI payments to households ubij,s,tubi_{j,s,t}ubij,s,t​ can be growth adjusted so that they grow over time at the rate of productivity growth or non-growth adjusted such that they are constant overtime. In the first case, when UBI benefits are growth adjusted and growing over time, the stationary aggregate government UBI payout UBI^t\hat{UBI}_tUBI^t​ is found by dividing (104) by egytN~te^{g_y t}\tilde{N}_tegy​tN~t​. In the second case, when UBI benefits are constant over time and not growing with productivity, the stationary aggregate government UBI payout UBI^t\hat{UBI}_tUBI^t​ is found by dividing (104) by only N~t\tilde{N}_tN~t​.

Stationarized Pension System Equations¶

Stiationarized Notional Defined Contributions Equations¶

The stationarized NDC pension amount is given by:

θ^j,u,t+u−s={0,if u<R[∑s=ER−1τtpw^tegy(u−s)ej,snj,s,t(1+gNDC,t)R−s−1]δR,t,otherwise\hat{\theta}_{j,u,t+u-s}= \begin{cases} 0, & \text{if}\ u < R \\ \biggl[\sum_{s=E}^{R-1}\tau^{p}_{t}\frac{\hat{w}_{t}}{e^{g_{y}(u-s)}}e_{j,s}n_{j,s,t}(1 + g_{NDC,t})^{R-s-1}\biggr]\delta_{R, t}, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}θ^j,u,t+u−s​=⎩⎨⎧​0,[∑s=ER−1​τtp​egy​(u−s)w^t​​ej,s​nj,s,t​(1+gNDC,t​)R−s−1]δR,t​,​if u<Rotherwise​
(167)

The stationarized derivative of the pension amount it slightly simpler since it involved only current period wages. We give the derivation first.

The FOC for the choice of labor supply is given by:

(11+τj,s,tc)(wtej,s−∂Tj,s,t∂nj,s,t)cj,s,t−σ+∑u=RE+Sβu−s∏v=su(1−ρv)∂θj,u,t+u−s∂nj,s,tcj,u,t+u−s−σ(11+τj,u,t+u−sc)=MDUl(nj,s,t)egyt(1−σ)\begin{split} \biggl(\frac{1}{1 + \tau^{c}_{j,s,t}}\biggr)&\biggl(w_{t}e_{j,s} - \frac{\partial T_{j,s,t}}{\partial n_{j,s,t}}\biggr)c^{-\sigma}_{j,s,t} + \sum_{u=R}^{E+S}\beta^{u-s}\prod_{v=s}^{u}(1-\rho_{v})\frac{\partial \theta_{j,u,t+u-s}}{\partial n_{j,s,t}}c^{-\sigma}_{j,u,t+u-s}\biggl(\frac{1}{1+\tau^{c}_{j,u,t+u-s}}\biggr) \\ & = MDU_l(n_{j,s,t})e^{g_{y}t(1-\sigma)} \end{split}(1+τj,s,tc​1​)​(wt​ej,s​−∂nj,s,t​∂Tj,s,t​​)cj,s,t−σ​+u=R∑E+S​βu−sv=s∏u​(1−ρv​)∂nj,s,t​∂θj,u,t+u−s​​cj,u,t+u−s−σ​(1+τj,u,t+u−sc​1​)=MDUl​(nj,s,t​)egy​t(1−σ)​

where we now pull the growth factor out of the marginal disutility of labor term to aid in the exposition of the stationarization. To stationarize this equation, we divide both sides through by egyt(1−σ)e^{g_{y}t(1-\sigma)}egy​t(1−σ).
